chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

In the case of a female slave who is contracted for manumission (mukattabah), and her master has sexual relations with her, causing her to become pregnant, he said: 'He returns to her the dowry of her like (i.e., comparable value), and strives to pay her valuation. If she is unable to pay, she is considered one of the mothers of children (ummahat al-awlad).'

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِ الْأَوْلَادِ: Mothers of children, a legal status where a slave woman is freed upon her master's death upon bearing his child.
key_terms.قِيمَتِهَا: Her valuation or price, the amount owed for her freedom.
key_terms.مَهْرَ مِثْلِهَا: The dowry of her like (comparable value), referring to the compensation for her status.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: A slave woman who has contracted to pay a specific sum for her freedom in installments.
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her (specifically in the context of manumission or ownership).

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a female slave who becomes pregnant by her master while under a manumission contract?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the transition of a *mukattabah* slave into an *ummahat al-walad* (mother of the child) upon the master's sexual intercourse with her, a status that grants her freedom upon his death. The requirement for the master to pay her dowry (*mahr al-mithl*) and strive for her valuation underscores the financial and legal protections afforded to her during this interim period, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the dignity and gradual emancipation of slaves within the family structure.
